The disappearing peaks are most likely an artifact of over-crosslinking. PFA alone is often sufficient for direct DNA-binding proteins like IKAROS. Adding DSG increases protein–protein crosslinking and overall crosslink density, which can cause open chromatin regions (active promoters and enhancers) to become heavily crosslinked protein–DNA aggregates. These over-crosslinked complexes resist shearing by sonication and can become trapped in the insoluble fraction, leading to loss of ChIP signal specifically at these accessible, highly occupied genomic sites.

PFA (paraformaldehyde) crosslinks proteins to DNA and protein-protein interactions. It is a reversible crosslinker, works for proteins closely associated with DNA. DSG (disuccinimidyl glutarate) is an additional crosslinker that crosslinks protein-protein interactions more efficiently, especially for proteins that are not directly binding DNA or are in larger complexes. Typically, dual crosslinking (PFA+DSG) is used to capture proteins that are indirectly associated with DNA or in large complexes. It anchors the protein complexes better.
